reason: OpenDataFile selects resource-file families; equal 0..15 indices in demon classes, condition actions, and text colors select different tables.

ActionWait.remaining uses ready, queued, reset-delay 255, and alert-clamp 512 tick values; ActionMark instead marks the separate ready byte.
skilluse.c stores default, condition, or battle-tally as the type of outcome reported after an action; BattleActionResult selects the message result code.
Character and field-object personal flag bitsets track noticed, anchored, invisible, Estoma, and battle effects; equal bit indices in other enums address other bitsets.
GetAlignmentClassB returns negative, neutral, or positive alignment; CellTrapAlignmentMask derives separate law/neutral/chaos bits from the class.

LoadWallTextures uses 6 for an unlit texture and 10 for the area-specific map override; these values select wall-render resources.

IsCellBlocked and CheckBlockingCell switch between drawing automap icons and testing a cell at x/y; the selector is a map-scan operation, not a level-list choice.
GetLevelList chooses the loaded level room list or door list, which FindRegionData consumes with different record strides; equal 0/1 scan modes do not choose these lists.
AreaNpc.directionMask and GetNpcImageOfCode use compass-facing bits 1/2/4/8; ViewDirection uses the distinct ordinal directions 0/1/2/3.
treasurebox.c dispatches these effect codes to field-effect helpers such as Traesto and Estoma; coincident item, skill, or condition values address other records.
The field-effect helpers return failed, none, or done to their callers; FieldEffectCode instead selects which effect to attempt.
Weapon, item, and skill attacks compare relative combatant facing with face-to-face and from-behind cases; ViewDirection is an absolute compass direction.

Skill resistance followup chooses reflection, suppression, or target continuation after GetActionResistance; BattleProtectionResult encodes a protection outcome with different zero and negative meanings.

Field objects store pleading, friendly, hostile, and normal attitude and use s_attitudeNames and scene choices; equal ordinals in ActorMode describe AI actions.
RunAutomapState advances an automap window through open, draw, scroll, and close phases; these values are not the phases of another game state.

Automap scroll values index a screen-relative up/right/down/left panel; RunAutomapState rotates those moves through s_mapDirection, whose ViewDirection values encode world-facing north/east/south/west. MoveCommand encodes movement relative to the party.
UpdateAutomapScrollPanel stores blocked map-scroll directions as left/right/up/down bits; the same powers of two in mouse or map flags apply to other fields.
The automap detail gate increases from no map to basic, NPC, and object marks; it is an icon-visibility level, not a menu or movement state.
The automap icon table in treasurebox.c maps CellCode entries to mark IDs and detail levels; a mark selects an icon, not the originating cell code.
SaveOrRestoreBag copies bag entries to or from script-variable storage according to save or restore; WindowColorStashAction addresses a window attribute and reverses the ordering.
FindBagItem tests ordinary and scenario bag groups as bits and accepts both; CombatantSide and other bitmasks choose unrelated collections.
SetActionResult stores the low battle-message result code from missed through protected; ActionDrainTag adds higher composite tags to the result word after drain effects.
skilluse.c ORs HP, MP, and experience drain tags 0x50/0x70/0x80 into g_actionResult; BattleActionResult owns its low message code.
BattleStatGroup indexes weapon, gun, magic, and demon-interaction statistic groups; EquipPart indexes worn equipment parts and only its first two ordinals coincide.
Character battleStats and battleStatsShown index weapon, gun, magic, and demon-interaction levels and values; CharacterStat indexes the separate base-stat array.
s_bloodTypes indexes the four human blood-type strings and the count; coincident 0..4 values in character or menu enums select other data.
Area-map cell records store these authored codes; the cell-kind and automap tables explicitly convert a code to event kind and icon mark, so those outputs remain separate domains.
character.c returns ready, blocked by condition, or action pending for a member pick; PartyMemberPickResult instead reports empty, unavailable, or ready from the battle picker.
GetPoolState classifies current-versus-maximum pool as empty, partial, or full; PoolFillMode selects a target cap for filling.
Character.mode directs field-object and combatant AI through attack, flee, defend, movement, idle, and talk; pickRole stores the separate chosen command.
InitCharacterSlot stores none, male, or female in Character.gender, later tested by script logic; these are character attributes rather than choice outcomes.
Character.pickRole selects a battle command and its record (attack, gun, magic, item, and others); Character.mode drives AI behavior and maps several modes to one pick role.
Character pool queries combine HP and MP bits to select one or both pools; the same bit values in combatant or bag masks address different resources.
Character base-stat arrays use indices for intuition, mental strength, magic, and further traits; BattleStatIndex addresses a different combat-stat layout.
AdvanceClock and TickClock return a bitmask of tick, minute, hour, day, and moon changes, consumed by ApplyClockChanges; MoonPhase is a 0..27 clock position.
TickPartyTimers reports inactive, unchanged, or applied timed party cost; these values are a timer result rather than clock-change bits.
GameClock.moonPhase indexes the 28-phase moon table and script switch, with named new, full, and after-full positions; ClockUpdate only reports that the phase changed.
AddCondition distinguishes already held, blocked, added, and cancelled opposite; ConditionChangeResult instead grades a later mild or severe transition.
Condition aging reports none, mild, or severe changes to sleep and related conditions; AddCondition reports acceptance and opposition of a new condition.
The empty-pool handler distinguishes HP dying added, already dying, other condition added, and combined cases; ConditionAddResult describes one attempted insertion.
Condition lists and s_conditionNames index named ailments such as ash, paralysis, and poison; equal ordinal values in skill, item, or game-state enums address unrelated records.
RunDdsSummon uses prepare, pick, and close as its outer summon steps; DdsSummonCursorStep separately tracks roster and party-slot selection inside pick.
PickDdsSummon advances a cursor through roster pick, party slot, transition, exchange, and finish; DdsSummonStep is the outer menu step.
PickDdsRosterMember advances an argument through status-list selection and returns -1 after closing; the fusion picker uses separate fusion menus, return codes, and a preview state.
PickDdsPurgeMember uses prepare, finish, and pick in its own purge substate; the order and actions differ from summon steps.
PickDdsSummon and ReturnDdsMember report cancelled, pending, or completed DDS actions; TargetPickResult reports target selection and DdsSummonCursorStep is internal progress.
ET0000 race-class map and class names define this domain; equal 0..15 file-kind, action, and color indices are unrelated.
GetDemonPantheon reads the character pantheon and GetDemonPantheonName uses the pantheon-name block; GetDemonRace reads a separate race field and table.
GetDemonRace and GetDemonRaceName select a demon race, and fusion searches compare races; DemonPantheon is a separate character attribute and name table.
fieldobj.c decodes low and high value/unavailable bits from packed demon-table flags; equal bit numbers in actor or panel flags address other storage.
Fusion getters report unavailable, clear, or set state; BitChangeMode tells ModifyEventFlag to toggle, clear, or set a bit.
g_dropSlots has sixteen drop records and itemrecord.c iterates that fixed slot count; 16 is a table capacity, not a state or flag value.
ApplyEquipmentEffects branches on stat-update, action, or step-tick timing; the values choose when an item effect fires, not an equip-screen step.
Logical part order is weapon/gun/ammo/head/body/arms/legs/accessory; GetEquipSlot maps it to a different packed equipment-slot order.
PollEquipPart receives reset, part pick, attach-target pick, or clear as an input mode; EquipScreenStep instead names the caller substeps.
RunEquipScreen uses substeps 3..6 to preview and apply equipment additions or removals after MenuStateStep; AttachScreenStep handles different target and item paths.
RunAttachScreen uses substeps 3..8 to open and pick a target then apply bag or equipped items; EquipScreenStep uses the same low numbers for preview and equip/remove.
RunItemPage and RunSkillPage share menu substeps 0..2 and the same 3/show-description then 4/wait-dismissal transition; the payload-specific drawing remains in each handler.
RunItemPage and RunSkillPage share menu substeps 0..2 and the same 3/show-description then 4/wait-dismissal transition; the payload-specific drawing remains in each handler.
Character equipment array order is head/body/arms/legs/accessory/weapon/gun/ammo; equal EquipPart values refer to different parts.
EnterFieldMap records whether a field encounter came from a cell event or script, with -1 inactive; FieldMapOutcome records how it ended.
RunFieldEncounter and RunFieldState advance through enter, turns, rewards, level-ups, analyze, and teardown; FieldEncounterEntryStep is nested inside enter.
The encounter entry phase uses setup 0 and start 1 while the outer FieldEncounterPhase runs the complete battle lifecycle.
LeaveFieldMap records lost, ended, or won for the current encounter; FieldMapMode describes its entry route and has a different meaning at -1 and 0.
partyaction.c saves, restores, and loads the first and second field-object layers; these 0/1 indices address layer arrays, not a menu or map axis.
RunFieldExploration dispatches field exploration through area load, cell entry, event handling, return-point, and world-map transitions; other game states own their phase values.
fieldmain.c raises, queues, and completes a field-object event through its own state byte; ObjectLifeState instead describes whether an object is active or fallen.
fieldmain.c reports in-progress, done, or blocked movement; FieldMoveState stores idle, stepping, or turning animation state.
IsOnCellMark returns off-cell, matching, or facing-different for an event mark; it is a spatial check result, not a movement outcome.
fieldobj.c selects front, side, back, acting, and reaction images plus mirroring and lighting bits; SpriteImageVariant addresses a different image encoding.
FindObjectAt and CountObjectsAt select any, matching, or other record kind as a filter; ObjectSlotState reports the state of one table slot.
CheckObjectState reports free, removed, or live table slots; ObjectLifeState separately checks absent, active, or fatally conditioned actors.
GetObjectLifeState derives absent, active, or fallen from layer and fatal condition; ObjectSlotState tracks allocation and removal of a slot.
StepObjectTowardParty receives continue or stop on reaching the party cell; these values are movement policy, not ObjectLifeState.
SetFieldMenuMode enables or disables field command-panel rows for four field contexts; equal 0..3 values in menu row enums select actions instead.
WallStops tests geometry or movement blocking according to its mode; WallStopClass is a returned solid-wall classification.
Field movement checks WallStops against WALL_STOP_SOLID 3 to distinguish a solid wall; WallStopMode supplies geometry or movement test mode.
RunFusionMenuState uses phase 2 to choose and commit fusion results after opening, while MenuStateStep phase 2 runs an ordinary menu and other states have separate phase payloads.
RunFusionMenuState reuses advance 0 and apply 1 while opening and closing the fusion state; FusionMenuPhase owns the outer open/close/select phases.
PushFusionMenu stores pair or triple picker and commit commands as the fusion selection step; FusionMenuLifecycleStep only advances and applies outer open/close work.
GetFusionResultKind derives over-level and already-in-roster negative errors from a FusionSummaryKind and roster checks; the stored summary field never contains these exported errors.
RunFirstFusionPicker interprets -1/no pager action, 0/previous, and 1/next as panel button IDs; FusionPickerState tracks the picker state machine.
The fusion picker state is shared by first, second, and third fusion pickers, including a preview phase and selection result codes; the DDS roster picker uses a different status-list state machine.
s_fusionSummary.fields.kind describes the fusion outcome or source transformation; GetFusionResultKind may replace it with a derived negative FusionResultStatus.
g_party.field.moveState records idle, stepping, or turning motion; PartyMoveOutcome is a return value reporting in-progress, done, or blocked.
GetMapValue switches 0..3 over area, level, x, and y of the current map position; SaveSummaryField selects name, level, area, or floor fields from a save header.
PushGameState stores an ID for the state dispatcher in statestack.c, which selects field, status, script, battle, and other handlers; phase and step enums are local to those states.
InitCharacterSlot passes HUMAN_* IDs to LoadCharacterCore and stores the same ID in Character.id, which is typed ObjectRecordId; both name records in one character-ID namespace.
Field-object and character records store a human title used by title-name handling; ObjectRecordId values identify individual character records instead.
g_statusCondition carries a skill or attack infliction code, including direct condition IDs and special conditional variants; RestoreEffect is a cure or pool effect encoding.
ApplyEquipmentEffects dispatches an item curse to stat penalties, drains, or conditions at a chosen timing; ItemPassiveEffect describes passive item bonuses and resistance.
Item records and bag slots use these IDs for specific medicine, jars, shields, and story items; SkillId names spell records and ItemKind describes item categories.
GetItemKind reads the record category (restorative, weapon, gem, and others); ScriptBagCategory accepts these kind values but assigns 0 to all and adds special filters.
Shop-menu substeps open, run, and close inside each game-state phase; equal ItemMenuPhase numbers control the outer state machine.
Outer shop game-state phases enter, run substeps, and return; ItemMenuStep numbers control the nested menu lifecycle.
itemrecord.c applies record passive-effect codes to stats, regeneration, and resistances; ItemCurse instead triggers penalties and combat conditions.
The reward click reader returns none, confirm, or right-button result for the level-up screen; ListMenuResult reports an open or cancelled menu.
RunLevelUp drives member choice, distribution, demon growth, and stat redraw after open/close; StatusScreenPhase and other states reuse only low ordinal positions.
RunLevelUp uses fade then restore steps inside its close phase; LevelUpHumanStep and LevelUpDemonStep govern different growth paths.
RunLevelUp advances human growth through counting levels, picking and applying growth, distributing points, and learning skills; demon growth follows a separate three-step path.
RunLevelUp checks pending demon growth, applies it, and finishes a level; the human path includes point allocation and skill learning.
RunLevelUp redraws the raised stat, normal stat, or returns during its redraw phase; those values do not select close or growth actions.
The area byte selects one of the disc map files and indexes per-area automap storage; cell codes and game-state IDs select different records and transitions.
Lifecycle flags set and clear field/world-map state; skill-use flags are authored availability bits read from skill records.
RunMoveCommand interprets forward/right/back/left and turns relative to the party, with a queue terminator 255; AutomapScroll instead indexes absolute scroll-panel rows.
Character.id and ObjectRecord.id store the IDs used by LoadCharacterCore; both human startup IDs and named field-object IDs now have this owner.
FilterPartyMember filters a roster slot by party-position presence or reserve absence in character.c; CombatantSide instead chooses party or field combatants.
PickPartyMember returns empty, unavailable, or ready for command input; MemberPickState checks condition and action-wait readiness at a different stage.
GetMemberPanelState chooses a party command-panel image for empty, ready, unavailable, low-HP, or fallen members; PartyMemberPickResult controls input eligibility.
PickRandomCombatant tests party and field-actor bits in partyaction.c; RosterMemberFilter tests party and reserve roster membership in character.c.
AdjustActorAction and random-attack helpers report none, handled, or attack queued after a condition action; BattleActionResult describes the eventual battle message.
AdjustActorAction dispatches a condition-action nibble; equal 0..15 indices in resource, demon, and color tables have separate producers.
The battle panel command ID selects fight, gun, skill, item, and further action rows; EquipPart uses the coincident gun index to name an equipment part.
CheckBattleProtection returns a temporary shield result to GetActionResistance; zero means blocked, while zero in final resistance means immune.
Final nonpositive resistance outcomes include shield and record effects; overlapping negative reflection values come from protection unchanged, but zero differs from BattleProtectionResult.
GetActionResistance decodes record bytes 251..255 into signed absorb and reflect outcomes; AttackResistanceSpecial owns the decoded values, so the byte encoding remains distinct.
The current actor/target pair yields party pair -1, mixed 0, or field pair 1; AlignmentSide and CombatantSide encode different properties.
RunPartyCommandInput advances through member, action, target, confirmation, and summon-position selection; its phases are not target-picker return statuses.
HasObjectInReach chooses vertical-or-occupied versus shared-party-cell geometry tests; the 0/1 values select test algorithms, not a reach result.
RunPickTargetWindow low bits select field objects, party slots, and roster list; TargetFlags bits select actor side, target side, and self.

RunPickTargetWindow returns cancel/wait/selected after combining roster, field-object, and party-slot selection; PickPartySlotTarget translates PollPartySlotSelection and can reject its confirmed result for range or hover conditions.
RunPartyReorder uses phases 2 and 3 to pick two party slots and then exchange them; equal open/close phases in other states do not carry this reorder protocol.
fieldmain.c returns blocked 0, walk 1, or door 16 for a proposed party step; PartyMoveOutcome reports completion of the active move.
Character and field-object pickFlags use bit 4 to mark a skill-bearing item action; equal bit values in unrelated record flags do not select the pick item.
FillPool chooses normal, ushort maximum, or doubled maximum cap; equal PoolStateKind values classify current fill state.
ApplyRestoreEffect interprets an item or skill restoration code, including 1..34 as cure targets; InflictCode uses the condition range to apply ailments and has different special codes.
ApplyRestoreEffect reports fatal-without-revival, effect-reported, or no-effect-reported into the shared action result word; BattleActionResult uses those numbers for other messages.
ComputeRestoreAmount interprets 253..255 as quarter, half, or full pool restoration; motion opcodes at the same values control palette, sound, and jump.
ReadSaveSummary selects name, level, area, or floor from a save header; MapValueSelector chooses area, level, x, or y from live map position.
RunCellScene uses GetGamePhase for a cell-scene state and restores the field, sprites, and world-map request at phase 4; RunBackgroundScene has its own state and restores a saved background screen.
RunFieldTextScene has a two-phase text-scene lifecycle; RunFrozenFieldScene has its own freeze/palette/fade state effects.
RunFrozenFieldScene restores frozen objects and palette in its second phase; the equal text-scene phase belongs to another game state.
RunPictureTransition fades out, displays a picture, runs its script, and returns to the field; other scene phases have different setup and teardown.
RunBackgroundScene uses GetGamePhase for a background-scene state and restores a saved background screen at phase 4; RunCellScene returns to the field and handles sprites and world-map requests.
SceneSprite.flags stores interactive and X/Y flip bits while drawing scene hotspots; panel and mouse flag bits address different structures.
SceneHotspot.kind distinguishes field objects at 2 and boxes at 3 in the scene sprite array; UiHotspotKind uses 2 for an NPC in a separate clickable-view array.
The script animation state loads, runs, and closes a picture effect; ItemMenuStep shares run/close numbers but opens and manages an item menu instead.
Skill record availability has a third field-battle bit; IsSkillUsableNow checks it against, rather than transports it into, lifecycle mode flags.
CheckSkillArea reports forbidden, field-marked, or allowed availability for travel skills; SkillUseModes describes declared field/world/battle use bits in skill records.
GetSkillKind selects behavior such as attack, restore, drain, and battle-stat effect from a skill record; SkillId identifies individual skill records.
The skill-family byte groups skills into Agi, Zan, Zio, recovery, and other families; SkillId identifies individual spells and SkillKind selects behavior categories.
Record cache and game logic use these numbers for specific skills such as Agi and Traesto; SkillKind and SkillFamily classify those records.
skilluse.c masks an effect code then maps power, accuracy, defense, or magic effect kinds to concrete BattleStatIndex slots; the two encodings differ.
The 0x80 lower bit and 0x7f kind mask split a battle-stat effect byte before BattleStatEffectKind dispatch; these are encoding masks rather than effect kinds.
Character battle-tally arrays use these indices for remembered seals, reflection, absorption, and other combat effects; BattleStatIndex addresses separate stat arrays.
The tally helper selects remembered test, explicit-index test, or remember mode; BattleTallyIndex instead selects the tally slot.
The battle action game state runs target collection, prompt, resolution, effects, and cleanup through its own phases; BattleActionResult is a message code.
statuspanel.c chooses first, both, or second stat-bar row for rendering; AlignmentSide shares -1/0/1 but describes moral alignment.
Analyze, item menus, and debug menu return finished -1 or running 0 to the game-state stack; ScriptStatus adds a separate yield value for script execution.
The dismiss-menu state resets selection, waits for input, then closes; StatusScreenPhase owns the surrounding status state and its member/command phases.
RunStatusCommands dispatches draw, poll, close, and status-page choices from GetGameStep; the DDS roster picker uses an argument and has only open/poll/close.
Status pages use none, cancel, and fixed-member cancel as negative control values; TextEvent and ListMenuResult use the same integers for different input stages.
RunStatusScreen uses phases 2 and 3 to pick a member and execute status commands; LevelUpPhase also picks a member at 2 but follows a different state and growth path.
The status member picker uses open, picked, poll, and a 0xffff cancelled step; StatusStep separately dispatches status menu commands and pages.
The status roster list filters all, summonable, reserve, and flagged member columns; its integers select list data, not a member-picker step.
The roster replacement state opens a list, picks a member, then applies the replacement; other three-step state machines use different storage and actions.
CollectTargets selects the geometric or visible portion of a target formation; TargetCountMode separately decodes the hit count and all/random selector from the range word.
CollectTargets extracts this count mode from the high nibble of range after selecting TargetArea; its zero and fifteen are count encodings, not formation areas.
Skill/item target flags choose attack sides and self; equal low bits in TargetPickKind choose picker sources, with a translation at callers.
StepViewCell selects the column or row coordinate to advance while traversing the view grid; ViewDirection selects a world-facing compass direction.

The party field position, field-view wall lookups, automap rotation, and world travel carry the same north/east/south/west compass direction; screen-relative scroll commands and view-grid axes are distinct.
StepWaitState switches on a phase for frame, input, timed input, or fade completion; WaitInputMask instead filters mouse events within the input phases.
PushWaitState stores this mask as the step of an input wait; StepWaitState tests it against mouse left-down and left-pressed bits, which use their own encoding.
GetMapWallKind and field movement read these values from wall data to distinguish doors, solid walls, invisible barriers, and passable walls; wall-stop modes select a separate query behavior.
The world-map handler in statestack.c advances through load, scroll, destination, travel, fade, close, and reentry phases; equal step numbers in other handlers belong to other state machines.
Bitmap decoders and color-key setup use palette entry 1 as transparency; matching value 1 in menu and state enums does not index a bitmap palette.
HasBitmapFileSignature compares the BITMAPFILEHEADER bfType against the BM file signature 0x4d42; it is a file-format tag, not a game value.
g_deviceType selects HAL, MMX, or RAMP rendering paths in bitmapio.cpp; equal ordinal values elsewhere select unrelated resources or states.
The motion command byte dispatches 0xfd/0xfe/0xff to sound, palette, and jump commands in motion.c; these are not the same payload as other 8-bit sentinels.
GetEffectImageBase is compared with 0x100 in effectdraw.cpp to adjust an effect frame; the value is an image-code base, not a script opcode bank.
vram.c sets and clears 0x40 dirty and 0x80 queued bits in s_paletteFlags; matching bit values in other flags operate on different storage.

UpdateAreaPalette and UpdateViewPalette store the same normal/dark material choice from IsDarkCell in two separate cells; the renderer uses either flag to choose g_roomTexture or g_darkWallTexture. This material mode is separate from PaletteUpdateFlags, which controls pending uploads.
The platform event handler tests scene picture IDs in the 0x50xx range to arm or delay the cursor; sprite composite IDs identify 0x40xx image operations.

g_renderMode selects one of sixteen s_renderModes frame handlers; setters choose the named modes and GetRenderMode returns the same value. The saved copy remains u16 because 0xffff marks it invalid after restore; this domain is separate from scene, game, and palette states.

s_blankStep advances from none to the first and second blank-screen compositions while RenderMode stays RENDER_MODE_BLANK; SetBlankStep supplies the same substep across game and script callers. These 0..2 values do not select the frame handler table.
worldtravel.c tests WORLD_MAP_HIT_MARKER_COLOR from the world-map hit result; 1 and 2 describe map hit kinds rather than UI row or input states.
g_screenLayers and ShowScreenLayer use these numbers as indices in the 15-layer display array; equal small values in other enums index different arrays.
ResetSprites uses this mode to clear all layers or only party and text layers; equal values elsewhere do not select sprite-layer clearing.
sprite.cpp tests bit 4 of the sprite image code within the 0x2000..0x2fff range for half-size images; other value-4 flags address different records.
The scene compositor treats these 0x40xx picture IDs as cached backdrop, inset, clear, and overlay operations; event cursor pictures are a separate 0x50xx ID set.
bitmapio.cpp indexes a texture material and diffuse-color table by normal, dark, and lit shade; these ordinals are not menu or game phases.
mouse.c and waitstate.c test the left and right button transition bits in g_mousePosition.buttons; same numeric bits in other masks operate on other fields.
scriptvm.c passes accept or ignore to SetWindowOption for right-click cancellation; values 0 and 1 are a policy choice, not a click state.
mouse.c stores -1 or 0 in the left and right click latches and consumes them; these values represent latch presence, not menu cancellation.
fieldobj.c uses 0..8 as positions in 3-by-3 cell occupancy layouts, with 4 the center; matching ordinals in other enums index different structures.
handle.c writes HANDLE_FREE or HANDLE_IN_USE into handle-entry flags and tests the in-use bit; equal 0/1 values in UI or game states do not describe allocation.

g_moveState stores one camera move or door-opening state at a time; AnimateMove uses the low nibble to choose a step callback and AnimateDoor resolves 16/32/64/128 into the corresponding 1..4 step. MoveCommand instead encodes requested party actions before animation starts.
winmain.cpp stores these modes in g_fadeMode and drives fade transitions; state-machine phases elsewhere do not encode fade direction and color.
scriptvm.c sends normal, immediate, or delayed actor alerts to OpSetActorAlert; the value selects alert timing, not an actor AI mode.
GrantActorSpoil mutates macca, magnetite, or experience; the battle-result selector reads totals and per-member experience or a drop item.
Script opcode dispatch passes jump or call to OpJumpScript and switch helpers; ScriptTestPolarity instead controls whether a predicate is inverted.
The script VM passes normal or inverted to conditional helpers such as OpJumpUnlessStatContest; ScriptBranchMode separately chooses jump versus call.
eventflags.c indexes sixteen saved FlagBank records; the same flag index can mean a different event in each bank, so bank IDs are separate from flag indices.
AREA_FIXED_BACKGROUND is flag 0x7b in EVENT_FLAG_BANK_AREA, tested by scene and script code; the bank and index together identify it.
Bank 7 uses indices 0xfd..0xff for shield and consumed full-moon items; identical motion effect opcode bytes select sound, palette, and jump commands.
scriptvm.c passes explicit or in-place mode to long-variable arithmetic helpers; those values select operand placement, not branch or test polarity.
scriptctx.c converts direct, character-ID, party-slot, and roster-slot references by adding a corresponding encoded base; these are input forms, not the resulting reference values.
ResolveScriptObject interprets the 1000/2000/3000 bases as party, roster, and character encoded references; ObjectRefKind is a separate 0..3 conversion selector.
ResolveScriptObject interprets negative references as current actor, battle target, fusion result, or roster slot; they are actual reference encodings rather than UI status sentinels.
scriptvm.c reads and dispatches serialized script opcodes to command handlers; equal small numbers in game enums select records, states, or arguments instead.
scriptvm.c adds 0x100, 0x200, or 0x300 after extension bytes to form ScriptOpcode values; these are bank offsets, not standalone opcodes or object-reference bases.
Game and script code tests these map and program ownership bits in EVENT_FLAG_BANK_OWNED; ScenarioFlag and ScenarioFlag2 address different flag banks.
Script VM find-member opcodes pass first-slot or slot-mask result shape to the same roster queries; the HP/MP pool masks are a separate argument to those calls.
Clock and item code test story-event indices in EVENT_FLAG_BANK_SCENARIO; ScenarioFlag2 uses the separate second scenario bank.
Field and status code test these story-event indices in EVENT_FLAG_BANK_SCENARIO_2; ScenarioFlag uses the first scenario bank.
Script character-reference conversion selects roster-to-party or other conversion direction; ObjectRefKind identifies the input reference form before conversion.
The item-count operator chooses bag, equipment, or their union; BagSearchGroup identifies item categories within bag searches.
RunScriptChoiceState uses GetGameSub to initialize its choice list at 0 and poll it at 1; SystemMenuChoiceStep uses GetGameStep and opens a two-row system menu.
StepForMode converts the script step request to a positive, neutral, or negative alignment result; AlignmentSide is the output sign, not this encoded request.
Script comparison code chooses literal zero or a decoded operand for its right side; ComparisonOperator separately chooses the relation applied to both sides.
ReadScriptOperand decodes the byte that identifies literal, variable, item-price, object-field, and action-result operand forms; ScriptOpcode selects the instruction that consumes operands.
ReadContestValues selects level, level gap, familiarity, or familiarity count beyond CharacterStat fields; StatContestLevel chooses a contest threshold tier.
GetBattleResultValue reads battle rewards, including experience per member and a first drop; ActorSpoilKind selects mutation of actor spoils.
GetActionValue selects which stored result of the last action to read: result, HP change, MP change, or drain amount; battle-result and action-status enums carry different values.
OpApplyEventFlag handles test, set, clear, and toggle as 0/1/2/3; BitChangeMode has only clear 0 and set 1, so their shared set value does not make one encoding.
